compare the bounds figure by figure

only figures common to both bounds can be relied on

compare Kai's lower bound with Leo's upper bound

the interval is 0.1 wide, but starts at 8.4 rather than being centred on it

The rounding unit is 10 kg, so half of it is 5 kg.

To be certain the lift is safe, assume the worst case: the boxes are as heavy as possible and the lift limit is as low as possible.
Number of boxes ≤ <sup>445</sup>⁄<sub>23.75</sub> = 18.73…
You cannot carry part of a box, so round down: 18 boxes
Check: 19 × 23.75 = 451.25 kg, which could exceed 445 kg, so 19 boxes are not guaranteed safe; 18 × 23.75 = 427.5 kg < 445 ✓

95 to the nearest 5 km/h is within 2.5 km/h: lower bound = 92.5 km/h

dividing, so use the upper bound over the lower bound

1.82162… × 60 = 109.297… minutes
convert hours to minutes

the upper bound of the time is below the claimed maximum

items.stem:
A rectangle has perimeter 30 cm, correct to the nearest centimetre, and width 6.4 cm, correct to 1 decimal place.
The length of the rectangle is L cm.

parts.t: Show that L = (P − 2W)⁄2, where P is the perimeter and W is the width.
Calculate the upper bound of L.
Calculate the lower bound of L.

Amal says the length could be exactly 8.9 cm.
Explain why Amal is wrong.

ms: The perimeter is strictly less than 30.5 (and the width is at least 6.35), so L is strictly less than 8.9
B1 for a correct reason referring to the upper bound not being attainable
sols: Perimeter of a rectangle: P = 2L + 2W
two lengths and two widths
2L = P − 2W
subtract 2W from both sides
L = (P − 2W)⁄2
divide both sides by 2
P lies between 29.5 and 30.5; W lies between 6.35 and 6.45.
L is greatest when P is greatest and W is least.
subtracting 2W, so the bound for W swaps over
Upper bound = <sup>(30.5 − 2 × 6.35)</sup>⁄<sub>2</sub> = <sup>(30.5 − 12.7)</sup>⁄<sub>2</sub> = <sup>17.8</sup>⁄<sub>2</sub>
Upper bound of L = 8.9 cm
L is least when P is least and W is greatest.
Lower bound = <sup>(29.5 − 2 × 6.45)</sup>⁄<sub>2</sub> = <sup>(29.5 − 12.9)</sup>⁄<sub>2</sub> = <sup>16.6</sup>⁄<sub>2</sub>
Lower bound of L = 8.3 cm
check: the nominal length (30 − 12.8) ÷ 2 = 8.6 lies between 8.3 and 8.9 ✓
The perimeter satisfies 29.5 ≤ P < 30.5, so P can never actually equal 30.5.
the upper bound is not included in the error interval
Therefore L < 8.9 always: the length cannot be exactly 8.9 cm
8.9 is the upper bound, which is approached but never reached
